purpose: Keep the accepted a20 actor fixed; transfer verified scene-residual diagnosis and background-protection practices from the historical 008 work.

source_workbook.extraction: Python standard-library ZIP and XML text extraction; workbook was not authored, recalculated or exported.

findings.a5_black_trail_A2_C2: Time-varying opacity, time-varying colour, material and illumination separation; representation resolution and illumination complexity also matter.
findings.a37_coloured_vehicle_residual_A3_C3: Object ownership, road geometry, visibility/compositing, and retaining or replacing old representation.
findings.blurred_yellow_line_A4_C4: Representation resolution, smoothing and road-reference colour; Gaussian scale/support and local boundaries.
findings.road_discontinuity_A5_C5: Road-reference colour and local scope/boundaries; freezing/joint optimization and old representation replacement.

cell_evidence.scope: Historical early Waymo road case, 49-to-199-frame road input and three-view optimization.
cell_evidence.finding: Near-vehicle standalone road coverage became 95.56%, while road contribution in the complete scene was only 26/19313 pixels (0.135%); existing static rows still blocked the road.

cell_evidence.scope: Historical early Waymo road case, three optimized views and 49 same-sequence inspection frames.
cell_evidence.finding: Editable static opacity plus road repair improved the supported reference region. Forcing more road transmission damaged protected output and had worse final reference error.
Optimizing a standalone road image did not ensure a correct shared-depth composite; added road could obscure valid texture. Final composite and outside-target protection must both be evaluated.

A frozen-model factor diagnostic in an early Waymo case found time-dependent appearance/disappearance affected the image far more than position changes. Use factor isolation to diagnose a black trail rather than assuming physical shadow.
Separate Gaussian colour/alpha, environment fill and final float RGB; zero Gaussian alpha can leave an environment dark band, and out-of-range components can cancel before editing.
cell_evidence.scope: The explicit environment-dark-band measurement is from Waymo scene one, not a verified cause for Scene008 or Scene065.

cell_evidence.finding: Use local old-representation replacement or controlled contribution, with protected boundaries. Too small a scope leaves the trail; too large a scope damages valid roads/vehicles.
Before-edit contribution coverage does not guarantee after-edit source coverage. Recompute contribution after removal; newly exposed sources are candidates, not automatically rows to delete.
cell_evidence.scope: The 78.08% weak-before-edit contribution statistic belongs to the procedural simulation evidence, not an observed Scene008 or Scene065 percentage.

selected_preserve.mechanism: Some pixels improve by reweighting useful original static contributions; other pixels need the road repair layer. Do not require every pixel to be replaced by new road.

strong_transmission_unselected.additional_objective: Negative log transmission through the complete static ray.
strong_transmission_unselected.reason_not_to_copy: Road contribution increased but reference error and outside-target changes worsened. The historical selected-C report explicitly corrected an earlier wrong branch binding.

correct_branch.transfer: Reuse same-sort diagnosis, selective local edit control and outside-target protection. Do not import historical thresholds, candidate sets, checkpoints, training budgets or entire-ray suppression.

transfer_rules.rule: At frozen actor/camera/scene state, split actual shared-sort premultiplied RGB and alpha*T by source, retain environment and constant-background terms, and verify float reconstruction closure.

Compare road standalone coverage, road alpha*T in the complete scene, and whole-group removal counterfactuals. A present but hidden road layer is an occlusion problem; an absent road layer is a supply problem.

Keep the accepted a20 actor, original source assets, cameras and trajectory fixed. Apply only evidence-backed context opacity/ownership changes in a reversible sidecar with exact native global row IDs; preserve the original/default scene.

Jointly check BUILD86/110 residual masks, all retained other vehicles, trustworthy visible road/markings and outside-edit regions. Candidate membership or ancestry alone does not authorize deleting a row that supports protected content.

Scene065_existing_K_union.policy: Existing complete native K-positive preservation union; do not substitute the 1831-row old-actor-source subset. Retained other actors also require their own full ownership protection.

transfer_rules.rule: After each tested removal/gate, rerender actual source contribution to detect newly exposed rows. Record one auditable global sidecar and fixed comparison masks, rather than accumulating untracked per-frame deletions.

If a trusted road surface itself contributes the red/grey band, diagnose material colour rather than deleting its geometry. If a wrong static layer blocks a trusted road surface, test selective front-occluder suppression. If alpha is absent and environment dominates, route the issue to the background/coverage diagnosis.

Evaluate the final shared-depth RGB, silhouette, real tyre contact/shadow, road markings/boundaries and protected vehicles across both BUILD frames. Greater new-road mass is diagnostic, not an objective or a success criterion.

implementations.reuse: Actual shared-sort source attribution, Gaussian/environment closure and entire-group ablations.
Pixel-wise source row identities and actual compositing weights with replay verification.
Independent edit-only gate with final composite and outside-target protection.
implementations.do_not_copy: Its broad finite-footprint candidate proposal, thresholds, loss weights and initial gate values are historical experiment settings, not Scene065 deletion rules.
